crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Common Sense
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The soul can perceptually grasp that there are two, three, or four nows, and their order of succession, without counting.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Common sense perceives number directly; animals do so too.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Perception
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: There is convincing evidence that Aristotelian perception can discriminate individuals by itself, without the assistance of intellect.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Two main reasons: incidental perception of individuals and perception of individual phantasmata.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Within-time-ness
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Beings who perceive time need not perceive the before and after in motion as countable in order to perceive time.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The counterfactual structure of time's mind-dependence separates existence conditions from perceptual content.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Principle
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle holds in Metaphysics A.1 that sagacious animals, lacking intellect, rely on memory for their capacity to learn.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Metaphysics A.1, 980a28 ff.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on δύναμις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The soul can perceptually grasp that there are two, three, or four nows, and their order of succession, without counting.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Common sense perceives number directly; animals do so too.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on χρόνος
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle attributes memory to animals lacking intellect, yet defines memory in a way that presupposes time perception.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle attributes memory to animals lacking intellect, yet defines memory in a way that presupposes time perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Recollection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The account of phantasmata formation in De Memoria 1 implies that phantasmata are fully individuated particulars.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle uses the signet-ring metaphor and discussion of memory defects to explain phantasmata formation.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Movement/Change
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In De Memoria 2, the pairing of motions representing events with motions representing time lapses requires that the motions be individuals.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: De Memoria 2.452b23 ff.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on State/Disposition
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle holds in Metaphysics A.1 that sagacious animals, lacking intellect, rely on memory for their capacity to learn.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Metaphysics A.1, 980a28 ff.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Imagination
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle appears to treat individual phantasmata of both objects and events as objects of perception in the De Memoria.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The account of phantasmata formation in De Memoria 1 implies they are fully individuated particulars.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on εὐδαιμονία
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Bowin proposes that the φαντασία enabling perception of the future is deliberative φαντασία, distinct from perceptual φαντασία.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: DA 3.11.434a6–15 contrast between perceptual and deliberative φαντασία
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Time
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: When Aristotle says 'the soul says that the nows are two', he is not talking about counting nows.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Counting (ἀριθμεῖν) is not explicitly mentioned in chapters 10 or 11 until after the definition of time at Physics 4.11.219b1–2.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Contradiction (PNC)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The existence of a discrete plurality of substances entails the existence of an intrinsically indivisible measure, guaranteeing such pluralities are always measurable.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Each substance in the plurality is itself intrinsically indivisible.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Temporalität
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Time's perception depends counterfactually on beings who count, but this counterfactual dependence does not require that perceivers of time themselves be able to count.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Distinction between counterfactual ontological dependence and direct perceptual requirement.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on κοινὴ αἴσθησις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The common sense in both animals and humans can perceive how many objects or events there are without counting them.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The common sense in both animals and humans can perceive how many objects or events there are without counting them.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Bowin, John

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Cause
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The verb ἀριθμεῖν (counting) first appears in Physics 4.10–11 only after the definition of time, and always in conjunction with being countable (ἀριθμητόν).
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Textual survey of Physics 4.10–14.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Temporality
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Time's perception depends counterfactually on beings who count, but this counterfactual dependence does not require that perceivers of time themselves be able to count.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Intellect
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In the absence of beings with nous and hence deliberative phantasia, time would be unmeasurable because no measure would stand in a measuring relation to it.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Continuous magnitudes require perception-relative indivisible measures; only deliberative phantasia produces these.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Bowin, John on Substance
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle holds that mathematical objects are sensible objects studied under a specific aspect (qua having certain properties), not purely abstract mind-constituted entities.

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Image
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle defines phantasia as a motion that cannot occur without sense-perception, arises from sense-perception's activity, and resembles perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on φαντασία
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle defines phantasia as a motion that cannot occur without sense-perception, arises from sense-perception's activity, and resembles perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on φάντασμα
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia is depicted as the counterpart of doxa because it provides a sensory representation of a state of affairs that exceeds the mere simultaneous reports of individual senses.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Insomn. 462a1: 'not only does it appear but it also seems' (ou monon phaneitai alla kai dokei).
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Imagination
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle defines phantasia as a motion that cannot occur without sense-perception, arises from sense-perception's activity, and resembles perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Perception
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle defines phantasia as a motion that cannot occur without sense-perception, arises from sense-perception's activity, and resembles perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Difficulty / Puzzle
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The major problem with 'phantasia' in Aristotle is not the lack of a single English translation but uncertainty about what capacity, process, and product the term denotes in each context.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Frede's own assessment of the interpretive difficulty.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Emotion
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: De Anima 3.3 presents a tension: phantasia is both a necessary condition of thought and defined as mere after-images of sense-perception that are often false.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on δύναμις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The matter-form analogy for phantasia and nous is dangerous because it implies a necessary relationship between them that Aristotle does not intend.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Unlike matter which requires form to be actualized, phantasiai can exist independently without being 'informed' by thought.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on κίνησις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle defines phantasia as a motion that cannot occur without sense-perception, arises from sense-perception's activity, and resembles perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Movement/Change
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The perseverance (to emmenein) of phantasiai enables them to supply after-images, memories of past events, and coherent dreams.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle explicitly assigns perseverance to phantasiai at DA 429a4 and Insomn. 460b1-3.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Presence-at-hand
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The dualism Frede attributes to Aristotle generates awkwardnesses that are unavoidable for any strong corporeal/incorporeal distinction.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The question of connection and interaction between corporeal and incorporeal necessarily arises for such metaphysics.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on εἰκών
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Because the intellect by itself is confined to intelligible forms, it requires sensible images from phantasia to evaluate concrete situations as desirable or aversive.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The strict confinement of nous to intelligible forms leaves it unable to directly access material particulars.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Phenomenology
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Frede's methodological strategy is to offer a 'minimal account' of phantasia's role in DA 3.3 and verify it against the rest of De Anima and related texts.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Self-description of method in introduction.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Destruktion
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's indirect, negative method of distinguishing phantasia in DA 3.3 is strategically motivated: he wants to secure agreement that phantasia differs from sense-perception before revealing that it has no independent faculty or objects.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The structure of DA 3.3, culminating in a definition that denies phantasia an independent faculty.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Being-in-the-world
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Frede's methodological strategy is to offer a 'minimal account' of phantasia's role in DA 3.3 and verify it against the rest of De Anima and related texts.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Self-description of method in introduction.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Care
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Frede's methodological strategy is to offer a 'minimal account' of phantasia's role in DA 3.3 and verify it against the rest of De Anima and related texts.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Self-description of method in introduction.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Being
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The dualism Frede attributes to Aristotle generates awkwardnesses that are unavoidable for any strong corporeal/incorporeal distinction.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The question of connection and interaction between corporeal and incorporeal necessarily arises for such metaphysics.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Soul
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The overall purpose of De Anima 3.3 is to distinguish phantasia from the other capacities of the soul.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Frede's reading of the chapter's structural aim.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Contradiction (PNC)
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's indirect, negative method of distinguishing phantasia in DA 3.3 is strategically motivated: he wants to secure agreement that phantasia differs from sense-perception before revealing that it has no independent faculty or objects.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The structure of DA 3.3, culminating in a definition that denies phantasia an independent faculty.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Thought / Intellect
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle repeatedly asserts that all thinking depends on phantasmata, initially without further elaboration.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Hypothetical Necessity
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle specifies that the suppositions requiring phantasia encompass any kind of thinking that assumes a state of affairs—epistēmē, doxa, phronēsis, and their opposites.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Common Sense
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In De Somno et Vigilia, the phantastikon is identified as the same faculty as aisthesis (perception), differing only in its activity.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on αἴσθησις
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: In De Somno et Vigilia, the phantastikon is identified as the same faculty as aisthesis (perception), differing only in its activity.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on The Unmoved Mover
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's final definition of phantasia in DA 3.3 entails that phantasia has no separate capacity of its own and no separate objects.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on τὰ ἴδια αἰσθητά
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: The phantasia following perception of a sense's proper object (idion) is true while perception lasts but can become false once perception ceases.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Aristotle's account of truth and falsity of phantasiai as dependent on the corresponding perception.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Cause
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle's indirect, negative method of distinguishing phantasia in DA 3.3 is strategically motivated: he wants to secure agreement that phantasia differs from sense-perception before revealing that it has no independent faculty or objects.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The structure of DA 3.3, culminating in a definition that denies phantasia an independent faculty.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on State/Disposition
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle expresses uncertainty at DA 432a31 whether the phantastikon is a separate faculty or merely different in being, and he never lists it among the soul's capacities in his systematic discussions.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on πρὸ ὀμμάτων ποιεῖν
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasia is depicted as the counterpart of doxa because it provides a sensory representation of a state of affairs that exceeds the mere simultaneous reports of individual senses.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Insomn. 462a1: 'not only does it appear but it also seems' (ou monon phaneitai alla kai dokei).
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Setting Before the Eyes
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle does not use phantasia to denote poetic creativity; instead he calls the poet an eikonopoios.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Poetics 1460b9.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Form
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle expresses uncertainty at DA 432a31 whether the phantastikon is a separate faculty or merely different in being, and he never lists it among the soul's capacities in his systematic discussions.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Substance
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Aristotle holds that when thinking immaterial objects, the nous has no nature of its own and is like a clean slate, becoming identical with those objects.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Aristotle

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on φαντασία βουλευτική / αἰσθητική
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Animals lacking phantasia would receive only a sequence of incoherent perceptual imprints, with no integrated experience.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Perception is limited to single momentary acts; integration requires phantasia
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on κοινὰ αἰσθητά
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Any panoramic perceptual impression that integrates successive momentary perceptions is already a phantasia rather than a perception.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: Perception limited to single energeia; integration across time requires phantasia
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.title: Frede, Dorothea on Recollection
crossPipelineHooks.bridge: Phantasiai vary in their history depending on whether they arise from immediate awareness or from long-term storage in memory.
crossPipelineHooks.relevance: The same causal account (motion caused by sense-perception) encompasses both immediate and stored phantasiai.
crossPipelineHooks.speaker: Frede, Dorothea

crossPipelineHooks.relevance: There is no separate faculty responsible for overseeing images.
